title: White society women playing with the band at the Harmony Club
summary: Allen asks whether society people sat in. Ridgley says young white women played piano and banjo with them at the Harmony Club, but men never sat in.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did they sit in with her, you know, and with you all and play some of those society people? Would they ever play with you? Who was that?
Would they ever play with your band? What you mean white?

Yeah white. Well sure we played at the harmony club then and they played, that's where at the harmony club, Jackson Cinchaw. Yeah that's it. We played there on several occasions and those girls used to play with us up in there. You know that guy.
Anything. Banjo, sing. Well they just liked us, you know. Right. It was always nice and clean and.
Did any of the men ever sit in and play the trombone or anything like that?
No, no, no, nothing like that. Excuse me, go ahead. Most of them like the piano, you see, the banjo, somebody used to put on with the bass violin and the drum.
Were some of them good? Oh yeah, some of them good.
